summary: Namco's horror beat-'em-up series, covering the arcade original, Famicom parody spin-off, Genesis sequels, and the 2010 reboot.

entries.title: Splatterhouse

emulation.emulator: Arcade Archives emulator / MAME if using original arcade ROM legally
emulation.notes: Prefer the official Arcade Archives release for a current commercial route; MAME remains the preservation reference for original hardware accuracy.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Arcade emulation with modern display options

primary.why: The original arcade game has many routes, but the Arcade Archives release is the modern official arcade-version route on current digital console storefronts. It avoids the censored TurboGrafx-16/PC Engine edits and is more direct than unlocking the arcade game inside the 2010 reboot.
primary.how_to_play: Play Arcade Archives Splatterhouse on Switch or PS4; use its arcade-emulation options, save-state conveniences, and display settings as desired.

secondary.what_to_play: Try Splatter Rush only if the delisted/mobile build is already available to you.
secondary.why: The iOS port added a mode where enemies continuously spawn on a wide screen; it is not the best main route, but it is unique content.

entries.remaster_caveats: No full remaster exists; many older routes are ports, compilations, or unlockables rather than a remake of the 1988 game.

entries.title: Splatterhouse: Wanpaku Graffiti

emulation.emulator: Native collection emulator / FCEUX or Mesen for original cartridge dumps
emulation.notes: Use Namco Museum Archives Vol. 1 for the official localized route.

primary.platform: Nintendo Switch / PlayStation 4 / Xbox One / Windows
primary.why: The Famicom original was Japan-only, while Namco Museum Archives Vol. 1 gave the game an official localized Western release across modern platforms with save/rewind conveniences.
primary.how_to_play: Play Namco Museum Archives Vol. 1 on PC, Switch, PS4, or Xbox One; choose PC for the most configurable display route when available.

entries.remaster_caveats: The international Archives release omits some Japanese Namcot Collection presentation extras, but that does not remove Wanpaku Graffiti's game content.

entries.title: Splatterhouse 2
entries.definitive_edition: Original Genesis/Mega Drive version via modern emulation

emulation.notes: Use an accurate Genesis emulator or original hardware; Genesis Mini 2 is the simplest official mini-console path.

primary.version: Original cartridge via modern Genesis emulation
primary.why: Splatterhouse 2 is a Genesis/Mega Drive game with later Virtual Console, reboot-unlockable, and Genesis Mini 2 routes. The original ROM through a strong Genesis emulator is the cleanest fidelity route without relying on discontinued storefronts or mini-console availability.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Genesis/Mega Drive version through original hardware, MiSTer, Genesis Plus GX, BlastEm, or a comparable accurate emulator; use the Genesis Mini 2 if you specifically want an official plug-and-play route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or content-expanded edition exists.

entries.title: Splatterhouse 3
entries.definitive_edition: Original Genesis/Mega Drive version via modern emulation

emulation.notes: Use an accurate Genesis emulator or original hardware to preserve the original artwork.

primary.version: Original cartridge via modern Genesis emulation
primary.why: Splatterhouse 3 was built for Sega Genesis/Mega Drive, and the 2010 reboot's unlockable version replaced digitized photographs with new artwork. The original Genesis/Mega Drive version is therefore the most complete/unaltered primary.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Genesis/Mega Drive version through original hardware, MiSTer, Genesis Plus GX, BlastEm, or a comparable accurate emulator.

entries.remaster_caveats: The 2010 unlockable changes artwork; no unaltered remaster is known.

entries.title: Splatterhouse

emulation.notes: Original hardware is the safest route; emulator compatibility should be checked before committing to a full playthrough.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: HD seventh-generation console output, potentially higher via emulator if stable

primary.why: The 2010 Splatterhouse reboot released only on PS3 and Xbox 360 and includes the original Splatterhouse arcade game, Splatterhouse 2, and Splatterhouse 3 as unlockables. With no PC or remaster route documented, either HD console version is the complete official route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS3 or Xbox 360 disc on original hardware; use RPCS3 or Xenia only if compatibility is adequate for your setup.

entries.remaster_caveats: No PC port or remaster is known to exist.

entries.title: Splatterhouse: World

emulation.emulator: FCEUX reported for the leaked prototype
emulation.notes: GamesRadar reported that the prototype initially required FCEUX because of an obscure late-era mapper.

primary.why: This is an unreleased Famicom horror JRPG planned around March 1993, later leaked as a playable ROM and fan-translated. Because there is no official commercial release, it stays as a limited exception instead of a researched best-version entry.
primary.how_to_play: Do not treat the leaked ROM or fan translation as an official release route; revisit if the rights holder publishes it commercially.

entries.remaster_caveats: Canceled before release; later public playability comes from an unofficial ROM leak and fan translation.
